text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski will pay a two-day visit to Slovakia, beginning on August 20.
- Slovakia's trade deficit with Russia totalled 22.9 billion crowns in the first six months of this year.

- A 10 percent increase in energy prices, effective from August 1, will cost oil refiner Slovnaft an additional three million crowns this year but the increase will not affect prices of Slovnaft's products.

- The state council supervising broadcasting of the official Slovak Television (STV) said there were professional shortcomings in the STV activities, mainly in presenting opinions of President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.
- The local banking sector on Thursday met its minimum reserves requirements after failing to do so for five consecutive times over the past 10 weeks.

SME - Opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) Deputy Chairman, Peter Weiss, said the ruling parties were now in deep crisis since they were not willing to respect rulings of the Constitutional Court.
- The ministry of agriculture has proposed excluding some agriculture products and food items from the new 7.0 percent import surcharge to eliminate any negative effect on agricultural production.

PRAVDA - Higher energy prices will not negatively influence Slovakia's sole aluminium producer ZSNP since the company has a long-term agreement with fixed prices and consumption volumes with the energy producer Slovenske Elektrarne.

- The Slovak foreign ministry and the ministry of finance are now analysing possibilities of asking for funds from a secret Swiss bank account belonging to Jozef Tuka, premier of Slovakia's Nazi puppet state during World War Two.
